svg.title: Proof. Restrict to the admitted subfamily x0 = 1. Then the target is global parity. Holding every other block fixed shows that the selected sensors in each block must determine its pair parity. In block zero, known x0 makes either x1 or p0 sufficient and at least one necessary. In another block, a pair-parity port suffices; without it, both raw bits are necessary because changing an unmeasured bit flips the target while preserving every measured output. The blocks have disjoint sensor scopes, so their independently necessary minima add and the displayed selection attains the sum. For full source reconstruction, each other block has four independent states and any two of its three possible binary ports recover both bits; fewer than two cannot do so. This proves its sum. Write q = ⨁︁ i>0 xi. If x0 = 0 it remains zero. If x0 = 1, the next bit is 1 ⊕q: it remains one when q = 0, otherwise becomes zero and stays zero. Hence all future readouts equal R after the first step, so one-step sufficiency is all-future sufficiency. Selected raw ports are fixed under F. Pair ports for j > 0 are also fixed; if p0 is selected, it updates as p′ 0 = p0 ⊕x0 ⊕R. Thus the cost-attaining augmented readout closes autonomously.
